## Summary

A follow-up tweet pointing back at Concretum's early-September 2026 piece **"How to Generate Alpha From Rebalancing Flows"** (tweet: it "sparked considerable interest among our readers"). The claim arc: **investors are increasingly receptive to the idea that the technical flows of large market participants can** [be exploited — text truncated].

What the framing implies (standard in this literature, and matching Concretum's SSRN body of work): large institutions — index funds, factor/smart-beta products, options-overlay funds — are **forced traders at their rebalance dates**. Their buy/sell pressure is driven by mandate rules (tracking an index, hitting factor targets, volatility targets), not views, so it is **predictable in advance** and **price-insensitive** at the margin. The alpha thesis is to model that calendar (month-end/quarter-end dates, Russell/MSCI reconstitution, implied rehedge flows) and position ahead of the mechanical flow. The attached image is presumably a chart from the piece (unOCRed).

**Article not linked in the tweet** — the t.co resolves to the tweet's own photo (`.../status/2100942817866461368/photo/1`). ## Why it matters

- **Rebalance-flow harvesting would be the third distinct flow-signal in the vault, and the most structural.** Captured so far: sector-ETF flow *positioning* as a contrarian fade ([[2026-09-14-p123-contrarian-sector-etf-flows]]) and crowd-positioning as fade signal in prediction markets ([[2026-09-01-polymarket-copytrading-filter-thesis]]). Those fade what the crowd *chose*; this fronts what institutions are *forced* to do. Forced-flow front-running is a calendar/anticipation signal, not a sentiment signal — different mechanism, different decay profile, potentially complementary to both.
- **Who's publishing matters.** Concretum (Carlo Zarattini & co.) publish SSRN-grade, methodology-heavy work (execution delays eroding alpha, capacity estimation, rebalance timing luck, factor-timing with momentum) — this is a research shop, not a course seller. Their "considerable interest" tweet reads as genuine traction for a flows paper, not engagement bait.
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) the article itself is uncaptured — no rules, no numbers, no backtest window verified yet; treat the mechanism sketch above as hypothesis, not the paper's claim; (2) tweet text truncated mid-sentence, so even the follow-up's framing is partial; (3) front-running rebalance flows is a well-tilled field (Russell reconstitution effect, MSCI reconst, month-end factor rebalances are documented in academic literature with shrinking anomalies) — the edge question is whether anything is left after costs and crowding, exactly the kind of question Concretum tends to address honestly; (4) media not yet OCRed — contents assumed chart, unconfirmed.
